comment: Native ICD-11 service capability — Existing requirements name generic functions but do not ensure that any offered server actually implements ICD-11's distinctive model and coding workflow. The conditional status avoids requiring every country or every deployed service to implement an unused standard. Evidence: WHO API (https://icd.who.int/docs/icd-api/APIDoc-Version2/), Embedded Coding Tool (https://icd.who.int/docs/icd-api/icd11ect-1.8/EmbeddedCodingTool/), Reference Guide (https://icdcdn.who.int/icd11referenceguide/en/refguide.pdf).

The conditional status avoids requiring every country or every deployed service to implement an unused standard. Evidence: WHO API (https://icd.who.int/docs/icd-api/APIDoc-Version2/), Embedded Coding Tool (https://icd.who.int/docs/icd-api/icd11ect-1.8/EmbeddedCodingTool/), Reference Guide (https://icdcdn.who.int/icd11referenceguide/en/refguide.pdf).
public.suggestedRevision: Insert row: Business process = Native classification and terminology support; Status = Required where ICD-11 is included in the implementation’s declared scope: ICD-11 terminology and classification support. Where ICD-11 is selected, the TS, directly or through a declared integrated service, shall support the WHO content model needed by the use case. This includes distinguishing Foundation entities from MMS categories; resolving their identifiers and releases; providing available designations, definitions, relationships, and coding guidance; and preserving complete expressions and their applicable postcoordination constraints. The implementation shall identify which validation and coding-assistance functions it supplies and which are supplied by an integrated WHO tool or other validated component. An implementation used for statistical coding shall apply the relevant ICD-11 rules; a code lookup alone shall not be represented as complete coding support. National conformance documentation shall specify the supported content, release, language, interfaces, and tested functions. A connection to WHO services or a local deployment may satisfy the relevant functions when it meets the same conformance, availability, and governance requirements.
